note: Both are the top-level definition of a real vector/linear space: a set of elements with addition and multiplication by real numbers satisfying the defining axioms, operations closed in the set. Apostol counts ten axioms (closure as 2) in three groups; Strang states closure separately plus eight conditions -> identical structure, only a counting convention differs. Chose strict-same with the bundled top-level definition rather than mapping s106 onto Apostol's separate axiom-group objects (a120/a119/a117), which are finer decompositions with no standalone Strang peer.

Apostol V_n = all n-tuples of real numbers with componentwise add/scalar-mult; Strang R^n = all real column vectors with n components, componentwise. Same space (R^n = V_n); only 'n-tuple' vs 'column vector' phrasing differs.
Counterexample: polynomials of degree exactly n are NOT a space (closure fails). Abstract-only; no Strang counterpart.
'Real linear space' terminology / emphasis that scalars are real. Strang has no separate object; s106 is the definition itself, not this naming note.
Theorem: uniqueness of the zero element. Abstract-only; Strang states no such theorem here.
Axiom 5 (existence of zero element). Subsumed within Strang's eight conditions but no standalone Strang object to match.
Notation for the negative -x and difference y-x. Abstract-only; no Strang counterpart.
Complex linear space (replace real with complex in scalar axioms). Strang covers only real vector spaces in this sub-block.
Example 12: solution space of a homogeneous linear ODE (a function space). Abstract-only.
Theorem 15.3: elementary algebraic properties (0x=O, aO=O, etc.). Abstract-only; Strang has no such theorem here.
Axiom 6 (existence of negatives, (-1)x). Subsumed in Strang's eight conditions but no standalone Strang object.
Example 8: continuous functions C(a,b) (function space). Abstract-only.
Definition of a function space (elements are real-valued functions). Abstract-only; no concrete counterpart.

Third axiom group (multiplication axioms 7-10). Content sits inside Strang's eight conditions (part of s106) but is a component, not a standalone matchable object; no relation among the allowed strengths fits part-whole.
Theorem: uniqueness of the negative element. Abstract-only; Strang has no such theorem here.
Second axiom group (addition axioms 3-6). Component of Strang's eight conditions (part of s106); part-whole, not a standalone match.
First axiom group (closure axioms 1-2). Content appears within s106 ('operations must produce vectors in the space') but is a component of the bundled def, not a standalone matchable object.
Example 7: polynomials of degree <= n (function space). Abstract-only.
Definition of 'scalars' (real for real spaces, complex for complex). Strang has no dedicated scalar-definition object.
